newsitem.title: Belgium: EU may clear Banco di Napoli package next month.
newsitem.headline: EU may clear Banco di Napoli package next month.

text.p: European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert said on Monday Italy's rescue package for Banco de Napoli went in the right direction and may be approved by the European Union executive in February.
"Globally speaking, the dossier is on the right track," Van Miert told reporters.

He said that in principle he had no problems with the Italian treasury's decision to accept a joint bid by treasury- controlled Banca Nazionale del Lavoro and recently privatised insurer INA to take a 60 percent stake in the struggling Banco di Napoli.
He said the bid had been given credibility because private partners were involved.

"This move can be considered as one which is comparable to the attitude of a private investor. We need some additional information in the coming weeks to consolidate that presumption," Van Miert said.
He said he would propose that the Commission approve the plan in February if he is satisfied with those details.
Van Miert said he was "reasonably confident" that Italy had handled the sale properly, selecting the best of two offers.
However, he added, "We need to be given additional information about the restructuring plan to be sure the chance to return the bank to viability is really realised."
He said the plan would be subject to monitoring after the Commission cleared it.

Italy's centre-left government stepped in to save Banco di Napoli last year after the group announced record losses of 3.12 trillion lire for 1995. The Commission began investigating in July a rescue plan that involves a 2.0 trillion lire capital increase, advances from Banca d'Italia and tax relief.
Van Miert said it was too soon to tell exactly how much money the Commission would need to clear.

INA and BNL have said they would pay 61.6 billion lire for the majority holding in southern Italy's largest bank. Italian Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said Italy would also sell the remaining 40 percent of Banco di Napoli as soon as possible.
